draftA:
Northwind Health
Attn: Claims Appeals

Re: Appeal of CO-50 denial
Claim: CLM-221
Patient ID: PAT-221
Date of service: 2026-08-20
Service: MRI, lumbar spine

To the Appeals Reviewer:

We appeal the CO-50 denial of claim CLM-221 and ask that it be reprocessed for payment. The service met Northwind Health coverage policy LS-14 on the date it was rendered.

Policy LS-14 covers lumbar MRI after six weeks of documented conservative therapy, or sooner with red-flag symptoms. Clinical note DOC-318 documents conservative therapy from 2026-07-01 through 2026-08-14: a course of physical therapy plus NSAIDs, with no improvement. That span exceeds six weeks and concluded before the 2026-08-20 date of service, so the LS-14 threshold was satisfied at the time of imaging.

Enclosed for your review:
1. Clinical note DOC-318, documenting the conservative therapy dates, modalities, and lack of response.
2. Northwind Health policy LS-14.

No change to the submitted diagnosis code is requested or warranted; the appeal rests on the documented conservative therapy trial required by LS-14.

This appeal is submitted within the filing deadline of 2026-11-18. We request that the CO-50 denial be overturned and CLM-221 be paid. Please contact our office if any further documentation would assist your review.

Sincerely,

Denial Specialist, Appeals Desk
draftB:
Northwind Health
Appeals Desk

Re: Appeal of CO-50 denial
Claim: CLM-221
Patient: PAT-221
Date of service: 2026-08-20
Service: MRI of the lumbar spine

We appeal the CO-50 denial of Claim CLM-221 for an MRI of the lumbar spine on 2026-08-20 for patient PAT-221.

Northwind Health policy LS-14 covers lumbar MRI after 6 weeks of documented conservative therapy. Clinical note DOC-318 documents physical therapy from 2026-07-01 to 2026-08-14, NSAIDs, and no improvement. This is six weeks of failed conservative therapy and meets LS-14. The date of service follows that course. The diagnosis code is not changed.

Please reverse the CO-50 denial and pay Claim CLM-221. This appeal is submitted before the filing deadline of 2026-11-18.

Denial Specialist
Appeals Desk

reviewOfA.strengths: The letter correctly applies LS-14 by showing DOC-318 therapy from 2026-07-01 to 2026-08-14 exceeds six weeks and ends before the 2026-08-20 service date, while leaving the diagnosis code unchanged.

findings.title: No letter date undermines timeliness
findings.detail: The letter asserts it is submitted before the 2026-11-18 deadline but carries no submission or signature date, so the payer cannot verify timeliness from the document itself.
findings.quote: This appeal is submitted before the filing deadline of 2026-11-18.

findings.title: Therapy duration not computed explicitly
findings.detail: 2026-07-01 to 2026-08-14 is 44 days, i.e. more than six weeks. Stating the span exceeds the LS-14 six-week threshold would pre-empt any payer recount dispute rather than asserting the conclusion alone.
findings.quote: This is six weeks of failed conservative therapy and meets LS-14.

findings.title: DOC-318 not cited as enclosure
findings.detail: CO-50 guidance requires a clinical-note reference; the note is cited but not identified as attached or available, which may delay review. Add an enclosure line for DOC-318.
findings.quote: Clinical note DOC-318 documents physical therapy from 2026-07-01 to 2026-08-14, NSAIDs, and no improvement.

findings.title: Ambiguous sender versus recipient
findings.detail: The header addresses Northwind Health Appeals Desk and the signature block is also "Appeals Desk", with no named signer, making it unclear who is submitting the appeal.

reviewOfB.strengths: Every fact used is accurate and verifiable: the date of service follows the 2026-08-14 end of therapy, the therapy span exceeds LS-14's six-week threshold, the filing deadline is correct, and the letter expressly confirms the diagnosis code was not changed.
